sentences.text: The single known skull measures 26.9 centimeters in length.
Its lower jaw is 26 centimeters long, a length shorter than the skull that is unusual for theropods.
A narrow, kidney-shaped opening on the side of the skull is approximately 5.4 centimeters tall.
The teeth in the front of the jaw have a unique D-shaped cross-section typical of tyrannosauroids.
Based on the skull size, one study estimated the animal was between 2.98 and 3.16 meters long.
Other researchers have suggested the total length could reach 4 meters with a body mass of up to 100 kilograms.
F. Lewis Bradley discovered the remains, and Arthur Smith Woodward described them in 1910.
Woodward initially placed this animal within the species Megalosaurus bradleyi.
The genus was established in 1926, separating it from Megalosaurus.
The name Proceratosaurus was formally given by Huene in 1926.
It was likely a carnivore that hunted relatively small prey.
Scientists suggest its low bite force and skull shape indicate it fed on small-bodied animals.
The prominent crest on its head was probably used for display.
In the 1930s, von Huene suggested a close relationship with Ceratosaurus and placed both in Coelurosauria.
The animal lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age.
The Bathonian stage spans from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
During this time, Britain was located in the subtropics and formed part of an island archipelago.
Contemporary dinosaurs in the Bathonian age of Britain included the theropod Megalosaurus and the sauropod Cetiosaurus.
Proceratosaurus is closely related to the tyrannosauroid Guanlong from the Late Jurassic of China.
It was debated whether Piveteausaurus divesensis belonged to Proceratosaurus, but later research rejected this suggestion.
